questions.question: Which topic is explicitly listed as protecting confidentiality, integrity, and authentication?
Which item is included in the outline of the presentation?
IP is described as what kind of delivery service in end-to-end delivery?
Which transport protocol provides connectionless data delivery on top of IP?
Which transport protocol provides connection-oriented data delivery on top of IP?
Why does TCP need extra logic over IP?

choices.C: Because IP is connectionless and TCP must create connection-oriented behavior

questions.question: Packets in the Internet serve the same purpose as what on a LAN?
Why are IP packets considered virtual according to the slides?

choices.D: They can cross multiple networks using different technologies

questions.question: The virtual packet is implemented by doing what for each physical network?

choices.D: Binding it to a MAC filter

questions.question: What is the usual size of the IP header area before options?
What is the maximum total size of an IP datagram according to the slide?
Which historical IPv4 class uses leading bits `10`?
Which historical IPv4 class uses leading bits `110`?
How many addresses per network does Class C have in the classful table?
Which field in the IP header tells routers where the datagram should ultimately go?
Routers compute forwarding decisions primarily using what?
To identify the destination network, what operation is applied between the mask and destination address?
In IP forwarding, the destination address in the datagram always refers to what?
Which of the following does IP explicitly not guarantee?
What is the minimum IP header size?
What is the maximum IP header size shown when options are present?
Which IP header field limits packet lifetime in the network?
In datagram transmission, which layer binds the next-hop address to a hardware address?
During multiple hops, what happens at each router?

choices.B: The datagram is unencapsulated, processed, and re-encapsulated
choices.C: The destination IP is replaced with the next hop
choices.D: The transport header is removed forever

questions.question: Why does IP fragmentation occur?

choices.A: Because network links have different MTUs
choices.D: Because ports can only carry 8 bits

questions.question: Where are fragmented IP datagrams reassembled according to the slides?
A TCP socket is identified by how many values?
In the apartment-building analogy, what does an IP address represent?

choices.B: The street address of the building

questions.question: In the analogy, what does a socket represent?
Which TCP flag starts connection establishment in the three-way handshake?
What does the server send back after receiving the client's SYN in the TCP three-way handshake?
Which TCP flag is used to close a connection?
What state follows `FIN_WAIT_1` on the client side in the closing diagram?
What kind of attack uses IP packets with a forged or buggy source address to conceal the sender's identity?
IP spoofing is most frequently used in what type of attack?
Why are spoofed packets useful in DoS attacks?

choices.C: They let attackers receive replies safely
choices.D: They hide the true source and make filtering harder

questions.question: What kind of trust relationship can make IP spoofing more effective?

choices.A: Machines trusting internal traffic from each other

questions.question: Which of the following is listed as a prevention measure for IP spoofing?

choices.A: Deny private IPs on downstream interfaces

questions.question: In a RIP attack, what false claim might an attacker make?

choices.C: That the attacker host has the fastest path out of the network
choices.D: That TCP has no sequence numbers

questions.question: Which mitigation is listed for RIP attacks?

choices.A: A newer RIP version with password authentication

questions.question: What does ICMP stand for?
ICMP is used by network devices mainly to send what?
What type of ICMP-based attack is described where forged echo packets are sent to broadcast addresses so all systems reply to the victim?

choices.B: ICMP amplification / Smurf-style denial of service

questions.question: Which ICMP traffic is explicitly allowed outbound according to the mitigation slide?
What does a Ping Flood overwhelm with many ICMP Echo Requests?

choices.D: The victim's resources and ability to process valid traffic

questions.question: Which mitigation is listed for Ping Flood attacks?

choices.C: Rate-limit ICMP packets or block ICMP at the perimeter

questions.question: What kind of data exposure is packet sniffing associated with in the slides?

choices.B: Sensitive information sent in clear/plain text

questions.question: According to the slides, what is the most effective method for countering packet sniffers?
Which attack category in the transport layer is described as making a service unusable by overloading the server or network?
Which transport-layer flood is listed as consuming host resources?
Which transport-layer flood is listed as consuming bandwidth?
In the DDoS slide, handlers are usually what kind of systems?
In the DDoS slide, agents are usually what kind of users or machines?
What legitimate phenomenon is contrasted with DDoS in the slides?
What problem is caused by lots of half-open TCP connections on a server?
In TCP SYN flooding, which handshake step is intentionally left incomplete by the attacker?

choices.A: The client's final ACK completing the three-way handshake

questions.question: What happens when the maximum number of incoming half-open connections is reached?

choices.D: Subsequent requests are silently dropped by the operating system

questions.question: Why is identifying the attacker in a SYN flood difficult?

choices.A: Because SYN packets are always encrypted
choices.B: Because the source addresses in SYN packets are often falsified

questions.question: Which command-line tool is specifically mentioned for detecting SYN flood symptoms?
What is the recommended value of `SynAttackProtect` according to the slide?
What does `SynAttackProtect = 2` additionally do compared with `1`?

choices.B: Delays connection indication until the three-way handshake is completed

questions.question: What does `TcpMaxHalfOpen` define?

choices.A: The maximum number of SYN_RECEIVED states handled concurrently before protection starts
choices.B: The number of routers in a path

questions.question: Which attack occurs after a source and destination computer have already established a communications link?
Which protection is listed as the best guarantee against man-in-the-middle sniffing of an existing client session cookie?

choices.A: Use SSL/HTTPS encryption for the entire website

questions.question: HTTPS is described as a combination of HTTP and what?
What trusted third party issues SSL certificates according to the slide?
At the transport layer, which two protocols are named as adding headers to the message?
What makes TCP connection spoofing harder than simple IP spoofing?
If an attacker can only send spoofed TCP packets but cannot receive replies for the spoofed host, what must the attacker guess during a new connection attempt?

choices.C: The server's random acknowledgment-related number used in the handshake

questions.question: Why is UDP easier to spoof than TCP according to the slides?
The transport layer is described as the last place to do what before segments affect connection management?
